A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same LightRetriever study with readable main text, equations, figures, tables, and complete Appendix A. Text and rendered-page comparisons support a reliable assessment throughout.

before.justification: v1 reports original query-encoding measurements, BeIR and CMTEB retrieval evaluations, and ablations in Tables 1–4, with dataset-level results in Appendix A.6.

after.justification: v2 retains the original timing experiments, retrieval evaluations, ablations, and detailed appendix results. Retained experimental outcomes qualify as original empirical results.

M1.justification: The Introduction revises the stated retrieval scoring from dense L2 and sparse Euclidean distance to dense cosine and sparse inner-product similarity. This is a limited correction to the method specification. Encoders, caching, aggregation, losses, and hybrid interpolation are unchanged; the PDFs do not establish an implementation change.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same 23 training datasets, 15 English BeIR evaluation datasets, and eight Chinese CMTEB Retrieval datasets. Coverage and task instructions in Appendices A.3–A.4 are unchanged.

E2.justification: Tables 1–2 and 8–10 retain the same comparators: full-sized symmetric baselines, Static Embedding, BM25, BGE-m3 dense and sparse, LLM2Vec, and E5-Mistral. No comparator is added, removed, or replaced.

E3.justification: The reported splits, decontamination, training budgets, model configurations, timing procedures, and nDCG@10 and recall evaluation metrics are unchanged. The scoring corrections concern retrieval similarity, with no separate experimental-protocol revision reported.

E4.justification: Figure 5 and Tables 3–4 retain the same dimension/sparsity analysis and ablations of KL alignment, encoder symmetry, embedding-layer training, instructions, and sparse token counts. Appendix analyses are also unchanged.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental run or seed counts, confidence intervals, standard deviations, or significance tests. The point-estimate reporting practice is unchanged.

E6.justification: All reported numerical results and qualitative findings are unchanged, including appendix results. For example, Table 2 reports Mistral Light Hybrid nDCG@10 of 54.5 on BeIR and 59.4 on CMTEB-R in both versions.

T1.justification: Section 2.1 changes its explicit similarity assumption from Euclidean distance to dot product, correcting its inconsistency with the existing dot-product objective and contrastive loss in Equations 1–2. The equations and Appendix A.5 derivations remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, Introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions and claims: lightweight query encoding, over 1000-fold GPU speedup, approximately 20-fold speedup without GPU, and approximately 95% retained retrieval performance.

C2.justification: Interpretations of model differences, optional KL alignment, symmetry ablations, and token-frequency effects are unchanged. Appendix A.1 retains the limitation that applications to non-LLM architectures such as BERT remain future work.

D1.justification: Section 3.1 and Appendices A.3–A.5 retain the same hyperparameters, hardware, data-processing information, prompts, optimization procedures, and pseudocode. Code and data access statements are unchanged.

R1.justification: The cited works and Appendix A.2 research positioning are unchanged. Introductory similarity terminology is corrected without revising novelty claims or the relationship to symmetric and distilled retrievers.

P1.justification: Localized sentence and terminology corrections appear in the Introduction and Section 2.1, alongside the updated arXiv version/date stamp. The title, abstract, section ordering, and appendix organization are unchanged.

P2.justification: Figures 1–6, Tables 1–10, and Algorithm 1 retain their displays, captions, structure, and placement. There are no substantive layout changes; edited prose only reflows locally.

improvement.justification: v2 corrects misleading similarity descriptions and makes Section 2.1's assumption consistent with its existing dot-product equations. These localized technical corrections improve accuracy and internal consistency. The experimental evidence, main contributions, and appendices remain unchanged, so the overall gain is limited.
